punchline: Canada's top young hockey players are unusually likely to have been born in January.
thirty_sec: In Outliers, Malcolm Gladwell notes that elite Canadian hockey rosters are packed with players born early in the year: about 40 percent between January and March. The reason is the January 1 age cutoff. At nine, the oldest boys are bigger and more coordinated, so coaches pick them. They then get better coaching and more games, and eventually really are better. Gladwell calls it the Matthew Effect.
question: Where in your life did an early head start get mistaken for talent?
